_comment: CROSS-LANGUAGE ORDERING AND ENCODING, pinned. Two places where Python's defaults were standing in for a specification, so a second implementation had nothing to be correct against.

band_bytes._what: beam.minhash: one LSH band's values -> bytes, as 8-byte BIG-ENDIAN integers concatenated, then blake2b(digest_size=8).
band_bytes._replaces: repr(chunk) (until 2026-08-04). repr renders the CONTAINER, so identical values arriving as a list, a tuple or a numpy array produced THREE different buckets, and group_signatures is typed Sequence[Sequence[int]] and accepts all three.
band_bytes._how_to_verify: concatenate each value as 8 bytes big-endian and compare with bytes_hex; blake2b it with an 8-byte digest and compare with blake2b8_hex.

vectors.name: small
vectors.note: four small values; fixed width means no separator is needed

vectors.name: zero_run
vectors.note: zeros encode to 32 zero bytes, distinct from an empty band

vectors.name: max_mersenne
vectors.note: the largest value a signature can hold (mod 2**61-1)

vectors.name: mixed
vectors.note: spans the range; big-endian puts the high byte first

leaf_order._what: beam.carriers: every carrier's poll() returns leaves ordered by (hlc, id) compared as UTF-8 ENCODED BYTES.
leaf_order._replaces: Python str comparison (until 2026-08-04). Python compares by CODE POINT and JavaScript by UTF-16 CODE UNIT. MEASURED with ids z / U+FFFD / U+10000: Python gives z, FFFD, 10000 and JavaScript's default sort gives z, 10000, FFFD. UTF-8 byte order IS code point order, so encoding first gives one total order everywhere.
leaf_order._how_to_verify: sort the leaves by the UTF-8 bytes of hlc, then of id; the ids must come out in expected_id_order.
